name: The Tallest Tree in Ireland, Powerscourt
age_estimate: not dated for this trunk; the estate puts its line of tall Douglas firs at about 150 years

location.address: River Walk, Powerscourt Estate, Enniskerry, Co. Wicklow

story:
The tallest tree in Ireland, by its owner's measure, is a Douglas fir on the River Walk at Powerscourt. The estate gives it 61.5 metres, or 202 feet, and likes to point out that this tops Liberty Hall in Dublin, at 59.5 metres.

In the nineteenth century most of Powerscourt's trees were new and exotic, collected from the Americas and further afield. The estate credits its Douglas firs, Corsican pines, giant redwoods and noble firs to the Viscount Powerscourt's tree-planting programme of 1870, and its mild climate for how fast they grew. It says a line of its Douglas firs, among the tallest in Ireland, is about 150 years old.

In November 2013 the Irish Examiner reported that this fir had been officially recognised as the tallest tree in Ireland since records began, at the same 61.5 metres. We have found no newer published measurement, and Douglas firs keep growing, so read the title as a 2013 record rather than a final one.

Finding this one trunk is the harder part. The estate does not publish where on the River Walk it stands, so the pin here is the national heritage-tree register's point for Powerscourt's one exceptional Douglas fir, by the River Dargle, which may or may not be the same tree. Nobody has dated this particular trunk either. If you have stood under it, or know which one it is, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its height, 61.5 metres by the estate's figure, above the other Douglas firs along the River Walk. It stands on the River Walk of the Powerscourt estate, by the River Dargle.
access: Paid. Powerscourt Estate's gardens are ticketed (prices not checked). The estate places the tree on its River Walk; whether that path is inside the garden ticket on a given day is not stated, so ask at the entrance.
transport: Powerscourt Estate is beside Enniskerry village, Co. Wicklow, about 1.5 km from the house to the register point. No public transport verified; check Transport for Ireland.
pin_source: Heritage Trees of Ireland record 437, the only Douglas fir 'exceptional specimen' at Powerscourt, near the Dargle at Onagh Bridge; a plausible, unproven match for the River Walk tree.
verify_notes: Owner page (Wayback 2025 copy, read 2026-11-06): 'The River Walk at Powerscourt features the tallest tree in Ireland, a Douglas Fir. The tree stands at 61.5 metres, or 202 ft, towering above ... Dublin's Liberty Hall (59.5 m)'; 'a line of Douglas Fir which are among the tallest in Ireland and about 150 years old'; Douglas firs among the species from Viscount Powerscourt's tree planting programme of 1870. Irish Examiner 2013-11-05 (read 2026-11-06): 'A Douglas Fir along Powerscourt River Walk has been officially recognised as the tallest tree in Ireland since records began. The tree stands at 61.5 metres'. Register row 437 band 100-150 (2009), not tied to this tree. Other heights (56 m, 57.5 m) and an Avondale fir at 61.3 m appear only in search summaries, not used. Alive: owner page in present tense (2025); no dated photo.

name: The Hackberry of Terenzano

location.address: Via della Rosa 11-13, Terenzano, Compiobbi, Fiesole (FI)

story:
Italy's register of monumental trees gives the Hackberry of Terenzano 182 years, which would make it some twenty years old when Florence became the capital of Italy in 1865. It stands on a country lane in the hills east of the city, 192 metres above the sea.

The lane is Via della Rosa, in the hamlet of Terenzano near Compiobbi, in the comune of Fiesole, about seven kilometres east of the Duomo as the crow flies. When it was measured in May 2022 the trunk was 4.5 metres round at chest height and the tree 15 metres tall. The national list gives a slimmer 4.05 metres, so the two tapes do not agree.

The tree is on the national list, not just a regional one, and it earned its place on two of the register's seven criteria, its age and size and its value in the landscape. It was not listed for its shape, its rarity or any history attached to it. What you come for is a big, old hackberry standing in open country.

The 182 years is calculated from a birth year the register holds without saying where that year came from, so treat it as an estimate. Its health was rated sufficient at the last check, and the register calls it accessible.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the trunk, about 4.5 metres round, on a hackberry 15 metres tall in open country. It stands beside Via della Rosa at numbers 11 to 13, in Terenzano near Compiobbi.
access: Free. On Via della Rosa, a country lane at Terenzano; the register rates the tree accessible. No gate or ticket recorded; the register's address is house numbers 11 to 13, so look from the lane.
transport: Terenzano is above Compiobbi in the comune of Fiesole, about 7 km east of the Duomo in a straight line. Regional trains towards Pontassieve stop at Compiobbi; the walk up from the station is not verified.
pin_source: MASAF / RAMI register coordinate (43.7806, 11.34721); no photograph geotag found.
verify_notes: RAMI record 14381 (read 2026-11-06, last updated 2025-10-14): Il Bagolaro di Terenzano, Celtis australis, national relevance, AMI 01/D575/FI/09, Via della Rosa 11-13, Terenzano - Compiobbi, Fiesole; estimated age 182 years 'calculated from the registered birth year'; health 'sufficiente'; accessibility 'accessibile'; altitude 192 m; criteria recognised: (a) age and size, (f) landscape value; girth 4.50 m at 130 cm and height 15.00 m measured 07/05/2022. MASAF list figure 405 cm, 15 m per the florence lead (not re-read). The lead also cites alberimonumentali.info for 'seen from the road in open country' and a main branch cut after a failure; not re-read, not used in the story. Age band 170-190 around the register's single figure.

name: The Red Mulberry of the W&OD Trail

location.address: W&OD Trail bridle path, Washington & Old Dominion Railroad Regional Park, Ashburn, VA

story:
Only five of the 32 trees on Loudoun County's Big Tree Registry have a thicker trunk than this red mulberry, and three of those five are sycamores more than twice its height. The mulberry is 218 inches round, about 5.5 metres, but only 45 feet tall, about 14 metres, with a crown some 13 metres across. The county measured all three in 2025.

It grows beside the bridle trail of the Washington and Old Dominion Railroad Regional Park in Ashburn. NOVA Parks runs the park along the former roadbed of the W&OD Railroad, a paved trail of 45 miles between Shirlington and Purcellville, with a 32-mile gravel horse trail beside it for riders.

The registry ranks trees on points, trunk inches plus height in feet plus a quarter of the crown, and height is where the mulberry loses ground. It scores 273.5, well behind the tall sycamores. On girth alone it beats the Shumard oak in Algonkian Regional Park, 33 metres tall, which the county calls one of the largest trees in Loudoun.

It is not marked as a Virginia champion. The county flags it as visible or accessible from public property, which on a public trail is the easy part.

Nobody has published an age for it. If you know how long it has stood here, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the trunk, about 5.5 metres round, on a mulberry only about 14 metres tall with a crown some 13 metres across. It stands beside the gravel bridle trail of the W&OD Trail in Ashburn.

official_register.name: Loudoun County Big Tree Registry (Dept of Building & Development, Forest Resources; measured 2025)

access: Free. On the Washington & Old Dominion Railroad Regional Park (NOVA Parks), beside the gravel horse trail that runs next to the paved W&OD Trail. The county flags this tree as visible or accessible from public property.
transport: Ashburn, about 10 km south-east of downtown Leesburg in a straight line, on the W&OD Trail itself, so you can cycle or walk the trail from Leesburg. No public transport verified.
pin_source: Loudoun County Big Tree Registry coordinate (ArcGIS layer, OBJECTID 15, TreeID 37); not checked against imagery.
verify_notes: Loudoun County Big Tree Registry ArcGIS layer (read 2026-11-06), OBJECTID 15, TreeID 37: Morus rubra, Red Mulberry, VA_State_Champ 0, Total_Points 273.5, Height_ft 45, Circum_in 218, Crown_avg 42, 39.04484,-77.48845, Last_Measured 2025, Public_ -1. Points check: 218 + 45 + 42/4 = 273.5, so the girth column really is inches (554 cm). Of 32 rows, five have a larger Circum_in: American sycamores 283 (127 ft), 252 (113 ft), 239 (121 ft), white oak 235 (112 ft), butternut 223 (71 ft). Shumard oak lsb_008: 184 in, 109 ft. The bridle trail placement is from the lead name ('on W&OD Bridle Trail, Ashburn', data/research/leesburg-rejects.json). NOVA Parks page (read): 45-mile paved trail Shirlington to Purcellville on the former roadbed of the W&OD Railroad; equestrians ride the adjacent 32-mile gravel horse trail. Alive: 2025 measurement. No age in any source.
